fdEvidence.error: Error: startup did not apply FD_CLOEXEC after trapped close_range

interpretation.blocker: After a same-PID exec of the installed read-only Bun, inherited sentinel FD 256 is still open but lacks FD_CLOEXEC when close_range is forced to SECCOMP_RET_TRAP. This is an unmet startup isolation gate, not a successful fallback.
interpretation.positiveResults: All 40 new spawn-native, spawn-trap, blocked-SIGSYS and SIGSYS-listener cases pass. Sync/async non-Bun toybox children cannot see the sentinel; parent FD identity and non-CLOEXEC state are retained; readlink has a positive child stdout-FD control.
interpretation.kernelControl: API 28/31/33 arm64 return ENOSYS; API 35 arm64 kernel 5.10 returns EINVAL for CLOEXEC; API 33 x86_64 kernel 5.15 succeeds and marks the still-open FD. The additional filter turns both close_range and an otherwise-invalid prctl marker into ENOSYS.
interpretation.sourceFinding: Pinned c-bindings.cpp startup calls bun_close_range(4, ~0U, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) and ignores the result. bun-spawn.cpp uses closeRangeOrLoop with a real close/fcntl loop after failure. Runtime observations match this difference.
interpretation.nextGate: Implement and source-lock a genuine bounded startup CLOEXEC fallback, retain the failing assertion, reproduce both ABI outputs twice, then rerun this suite before full experimental Binder/device expansion.
interpretation.bounds: The 1500 ms timeout fixture, 1024-byte output fixture, 100 ms readiness cancellation, 200 ms SIGTERM grace and 2000 ms reaping gates are unchanged. Only the fixed source-bound FD fixture gets 16 KiB of source; existing inline probes remain at 8 KiB.
interpretation.signalScope: The additional filter affects the calling Bun thread and inherited children, not other pre-existing threads or the supervisor. It adds restrictions without weakening Android/system policy. Blocked-SIGSYS spawnSync verifies post-exec child and caller masks; async spawn runs after the caller mask is restored.
noOverclaim: Not a security sandbox or a proof for arbitrary detached descendants.
No proof for FD values at/above the existing 65536 spawn-loop ceiling, CLOSE_RANGE_UNSHARE, all process threads, watch/reload, other syscall fallbacks, or ordinary SIGSYS default termination.
No API 29/30/32 application or full experimental Binder results and no patched/native 16 KiB execution claim.
This test-only result does not establish an actual production Binder/PFD leak or modify the official API 33 runtime or released v0.2.0 assets.
